title: Network mocking with page.route
summary: Mock GET /api/todos to show exact data, and mock a 500 to test the error state the real API never gives you on demand.
why: Mocking lets you test edge cases (empty lists, server errors, slow responses) deterministically, without changing the backend.
objectives: page.route('**/api/todos', route => route.fulfill({ json: … })) before page.goto
Assert the two mocked todos and '1 items left'
Second test: fulfill with status 500 → the alert 'Could not load todos. Please try again.'
pitfalls: Registering the route after page.goto — the request already happened.
Mocking so much that you no longer test anything real.
teachAlong: Cause: the route intercepts the page's fetch.
Effect: the UI renders your data or your error.
Gate: a planted bug ignores the API data — your mocked-data assertions must catch it.

requires.reason: Didn't mock the route: call page.route('**/api/todos', …) before page.goto so the page receives your data.
Answer the intercepted request with route.fulfill({ json: … }) (or { status: 500 }).

mutants.reason: the todo page ignores the API response

wrongSolutions.label: no mocking (real seed data)
